League of Women Voters hosts forum for City Council candidates

By Jake Lannon · October 7, 2026 · 1 min read

The Piedmont League of Women Voters hosted a Candidates Forum on Tuesday, September 29. The hour-long forum asked candidates running for City Council to respond to many of the community’s pressing questions. The five candidates running for three positions are Nancy Beninati, Adam Hundt, Tom Ramsey, Bill Reichle and Sunny Bostrom-Fleming.

For the first time in over six years, the LWVP hosted the forum in person for the community to attend. The forum was held in the City Council chambers of City Hall and was broadcast live through the league’s YouTube channel and KCOM.

LWVP volunteers Jennifer Giessler and Kathleen Quenneville served as moderator and timekeeper. The forum allowed each candidate to provide a two-minute opening statement introducing themselves, their credentials, and why they’re running for City Council.

After the opening statements, candidates were numbered 1 through 5, and the moderator called on them at random to answer each question. The candidates had a minute and a half to answer each question.

The questions were chosen from a public submission form and reviewed to ensure a wide range of topics. The forum asked candidates questions about Piedmont’s community, the budget, capital projects, infrastructure, disaster preparedness, and Automated Licence Plate Reader (ALPR) camera privacy.

At the end of the questioning period, each candidates presented a one-minute closing statement describing why Piedmont citizens should vote for them and directed the audience to resources that would inform them of their positions.

To watch the full forum and hear the candidates’ responses, readers can go to the LWVP’s YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/@lwvpiedmont/featured.

Visit the Election Resources page (https://bit.ly/4ymy5xS) to learn about what’s on the ballot and how, when, and where to vote. Ballots started going out to every registered voter on October 5. Ballot drop-off locations will open October 6. If you have moved or changed your party or your name, you can update your registration online. The last day to register to vote is October 19.
